mainTopic: Keeping the gifts when a כהן sells his animal, who the כהן claims from, and how doubts about a convert's obligations are decided
overview: The גמרא first tests the rule that a כהן who sells his animal 'חוץ מן המתנות' keeps the gifts. It explains that 'חוץ' holds the gifts back, while whether 'על מנת' does so is a מחלוקת between two ברייתות. Next, רב and רב אסי argue whether a כהן can also claim the maw from the butcher who weighed the innards. The גמרא traces their argument to whether מתנות כהונה can be stolen. A new משנה rules that a גר whose cow was slaughtered before he converted is exempt from the gifts, and in a case of doubt he is also exempt. ריש לקיש challenges this from רבי מאיר's rule that doubtful לקט goes to the poor, and he rejects רבי יוחנן's answer. רבא explains that the cow starts out exempt while standing grain starts out obligated. When אביי asks about a convert's חלה, רבא answers that doubts about a prohibition are strict and doubts about money are lenient. רב חסדא's list of a convert's eight doubts supports this, and the four exempt cases continue on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא where the condition does not keep the gifts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a כהן sold his animal 'on condition that the gifts are mine', yet the buyer may give the gifts to any כהן he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a contradiction: if a כהן sells his animal and says 'on condition that the gifts are mine', the buyer gives the gifts to any כהן he wants!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier rule that a כהן selling 'חוץ מן המתנות' keeps the gifts. It quotes a ברייתא where a כהן tried to keep the gifts and did not succeed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that a כהן who sells his animal can hold onto the gifts. This ברייתא shows a כהן who also tried to keep them, but the buyer still gives them to whatever כהן he chooses. So it looks like a כהן cannot keep the gifts after selling.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that; a stipulation attached to a sale
The priestly gifts (foreleg, jaw, maw) taken from a slaughtered animal
To any כהן he wants

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: "On condition that the gifts are mine"
phrases.notes: This is a כהן selling his animal to a ישראל and trying to keep the gifts for himself.

phrases.english: he gives them to any priest he wants!
phrases.notes: "He" is the buyer. He still has to give the gifts, just not necessarily to the seller.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule, stated just before this section, that a כהן who sells 'חוץ מן המתנות' keeps the gifts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a selling כהן can keep the gifts for himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows a כהן who tried to keep the gifts through a condition, and the condition did not work.

steps.title: 'Except' holds back, 'on condition' does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'חוץ' (except) means the gifts were never sold. 'על מנת' is only a request that the buyer hand them over.
steps.simpleTranslation: You contradict 'on condition' with 'except'? 'Except' is holding back. 'On condition' is not holding back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two cases use different wording, so there is no contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'חוץ' cuts the gifts out of the sale, so the כהן still owns them. Saying 'על מנת' sells everything and then asks the buyer to give the gifts back. A כהן cannot make such a demand, so the buyer owns the gifts and may give them to any כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Except; leaving something out of the sale
A holding-back; keeping part of the item for yourself
You are raising a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: Both phrases sound alike in English, since both seem to 'keep' the gifts. The גמרא's point is that only 'חוץ' leaves them out of the sale. 'על מנת' sells everything and then adds a condition.

phrases.english: Are you contradicting "on condition" with "except"?
"Except" is a holding-back,
"on condition" is not a holding-back.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עַל מְנָת״ אַ״חוּץ״ קָא רָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 1 by telling the two phrasings apart.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by their wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא with 'על מנת' seemed to contradict the rule about 'חוץ'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חוץ' keeps the gifts with the כהן. 'על מנת' does not, so the two rulings fit together.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: 'on condition' does keep the gifts
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא rules that with 'על מנת שהמתנות שלי' the gifts do belong to the selling כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a contradiction: 'on condition that the gifts are mine' means the gifts are his!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. Another ברייתא treats 'על מנת' as keeping the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said 'על מנת' is not a holding-back. Now a ברייתא says that with the very same words the gifts stay with the כהן. So the two ברייתות seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts are his, meaning they belong to the selling כהן
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: "On condition that the gifts are mine"
the gifts are his!
phrases.notes: "His" means the כהן who sold the animal. The buyer must give the gifts to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 2 and sets one ברייתא against the other.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'על מנת' is not a holding-back
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא explicitly gives the gifts to the selling כהן when he said 'על מנת'.

steps.title: The two ברייתות disagree about 'on condition'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנאים of the two ברייתות argue: one holds 'על מנת' is a holding-back, and the other holds it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about this. One Sage holds 'on condition' is a holding-back, and the other Sage holds 'on condition' is not a holding-back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות really do argue with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to make the ברייתות agree. The second ברייתא holds 'על מנת' keeps the gifts with the כהן. The first holds it does not. Either way, the משנה's 'חוץ' case is safe, because everyone agrees 'חוץ' holds the gifts back.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree about this very point
One Sage holds

steps.whatToRemember: 'חוץ' always holds the gifts back. Whether 'על מנת' also does is a מחלוקת between the תנאים of the two ברייתות.

phrases.english: They disagree about this:
one Sage holds "on condition" is a holding-back,
phrases.notes: This is the second ברייתא, where the gifts stay with the כהן.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר ״עַל מְנָת״ – לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds "on condition" is not a holding-back.
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא, where the buyer gives the gifts to any כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by explaining that the two ברייתות hold opposite views.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining it as a מחלוקת between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed all sources should agree on what 'על מנת' means.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנאים argue about 'על מנת', so the two ברייתות are simply two opinions.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about buying the innards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה about someone who asks a butcher to sell him a cow's innards.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Sell me the innards' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה. This line sets up רב's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a buyer gets the innards, which include the maw (one of the gifts). If he bought them without weighing, he gives the maw to the כהן and does not deduct its value from the price. If he bought by weight, he gives the maw and deducts its value from what he pays the butcher.

keyTerms.meaning: Its innards; the inner organs of the cow
The maw (stomach), one of the three priestly gifts
And so on; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מְכוֹר לִי בְּנֵי מֵעֶיהָ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: He said to him: Sell me its innards, etc.
phrases.notes: A buyer is talking to a butcher who slaughtered a cow. The innards include the maw, which belongs to the כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מְכוֹר לִי בְּנֵי מֵעֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of conditions and starts a new section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer of innards gives the maw to the כהן. He deducts its value from the price only if he bought by weight.

steps.title: רב: if the butcher weighed, the butcher can also be claimed from
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה is talking about a buyer who weighed for himself. If the butcher did the weighing, the כהן can also take his case to the butcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They taught this only when he weighed for himself. But if the butcher weighed for him, the claim is also with the butcher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב limits the משנה's case of buying by weight. He adds a new rule for when the butcher did the weighing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the buyer weighs the innards himself, the maw is fully his responsibility, so the כהן claims it from him. When the butcher weighs, the butcher is also involved in the sale of the maw. So the כהן may claim from either the butcher or the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of; a phrase that limits a ruling
Weighed
Butcher
The claim is with; the person who can be taken to court

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁקַל לְעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: Rav said: They taught this only where he weighed for himself,
phrases.notes: "He" is the buyer, who weighed the innards on his own.

phrases.english: but if the butcher weighed for him,
the claim is with the butcher.
phrases.notes: In this case the כהן can go after the butcher too, not only the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁקַל לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case of the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the buyer weighed, the כהן claims from the buyer. If the butcher weighed, the כהן may also claim from the butcher.

steps.title: רב אסי: the claim is always with the buyer
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי disagrees with רב. Even when the butcher weighed, the כהן claims only from the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said: Even if the butcher weighed for him, the claim is with him, the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives an opinion that argues with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אסי, who did the weighing makes no difference. The buyer has the maw, so only the buyer must answer to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
With him; here, the buyer

steps.whatToRemember: רב: if the butcher weighed, the כהן may claim from the butcher as well. רב אסי: the כהן claims only from the buyer, no matter who weighed.

phrases.english: And Rav Asi said:
Even if the butcher weighed for him,
the claim is with him.
phrases.notes: "Him" means the buyer, not the butcher. That is the difference from רב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שָׁקַל לוֹ טַבָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רב's limit from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the butcher weighed, the כהן claims the maw only from the buyer.

steps.title: Suggesting the argument depends on רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב and רב אסי argue about רב חסדא's rule that a robbery victim may collect from either the robber or the person who ate the stolen item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say they argue about the rule of רב חסדא. רב חסדא said: if someone robbed an item, the owners had not yet given up hope of getting it back, and then another person came and ate it, the owner can collect from whichever one he wants. So one master (רב) agrees with רב חסדא, and one master (רב אסי) does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to explain the root of the argument between רב and רב אסי by linking it to a known rule of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The butcher who weighed the innards is like the robber, and the buyer who took them is like the second person who ate the stolen item. רב lets the כהן claim from either one, which fits רב חסדא. רב אסי lets him claim only from the buyer, so it looks like he rejects רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us say': the גמרא offers a suggestion that it may later reject
The owners gave up hope of getting their item back (יֵאוּשׁ)
Collects payment
He holds of / he does not hold of (a certain rule)

phrases.english: Let us say they argue about the rule of Rav Chisda,
as Rav Chisda said:
If someone robbed, and the owners had not given up hope,
and another person came and ate it,
if he wants, he collects from this one,
phrases.notes: The owner can go after the robber...

phrases.english: if he wants, he collects from that one.
phrases.notes: ...or after the person who ate it.

phrases.english: So one master holds like Rav Chisda,
phrases.notes: This is רב, who lets the כהן claim from the butcher too.

phrases.english: and the other master does not hold like Rav Chisda.
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי, who says only the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the underlying reason behind the רב / רב אסי argument from Steps 6-7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What deeper principle is behind the argument between רב and רב אסי?

steps.title: Everyone accepts רב חסדא; the real question is whether the gifts can be stolen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: both agree with רב חסדא, and they argue about whether מתנות כהונה can be 'stolen' at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone accepts רב חסדא's rule. Here they argue about whether מתנות כהונה can be stolen: one master holds they can be stolen, and the other holds they cannot be stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion and gives a different root for the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds the gifts can be stolen, so the butcher is like a robber and still responsible, and the כהן may claim from him or the buyer. רב אסי holds the gifts cannot be stolen, so the butcher is not a robber at all, and only the buyer who has the gifts must give them. רב חסדא's rule only matters once there is real robbery.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone (both sides agree)
The gifts given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal: the foreleg, the jaw and the maw
Can be stolen (count as a real robbery)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree רב חסדא's rule is true. The argument is not about the rule itself, but whether taking מתנות כהונה even counts as stealing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the argument depends on the legal status of מתנות כהונה, not on general rules of robbery.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: No, everyone holds like Rav Chisda,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּמַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה נִגְזָלוֹת קָא מִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: and here they argue about whether priestly gifts can be stolen,
one master holds they can be stolen,
phrases.notes: This is רב.

phrases.english: and the other master holds they cannot be stolen.
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of Step 8 and gives a different basis for the argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רב אסי disagrees with רב חסדא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be explained without anyone rejecting רב חסדא: it depends on whether מתנות כהונה can be stolen.

steps.title: Another version: the argument taught on its own
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the dispute about whether מתנות כהונה can be stolen as a separate argument between רב and רב אסי, not tied to the butcher case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this ruling on its own: רב says מתנות כהונה can be stolen, and רב אסי says מתנות כהונה cannot be stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another way this teaching was passed down: as a direct, stand-alone argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the dispute is not an explanation of the butcher case. It is simply stated as a basic argument about the status of מתנות כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (another version)
A teaching / ruling
On its own, by itself

steps.whatToRemember: רב: מתנות כהונה can be stolen (the כהן may claim from butcher or buyer). רב אסי: they cannot be stolen (claim only from the one who has them).

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ:
phrases.english: Some teach this ruling on its own:
Rav said: priestly gifts can be stolen,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה אֵין נִגְזָלוֹת.
phrases.english: and Rav Asi said: priestly gifts cannot be stolen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of how the dispute from Step 9 was taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: מתנות כהונה can be stolen; רב אסי: they cannot be stolen.

steps.title: New משנה: a convert's cow slaughtered before or after his conversion
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a גר is exempt from the gifts if his cow was slaughtered before he converted, obligated if after, and exempt if unsure, because the one claiming must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A גר converted and he had a cow. If it was slaughtered before he converted, he is exempt. If after he converted, he is obligated. If it is unclear, he is exempt, because whoever wants to take money from his fellow must bring the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, about when a convert must give מתנות כהונה from his cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before conversion he was not Jewish, so the gifts did not apply. After conversion he is like any Jew and must give. When we don't know, the כהן is the one trying to take from the גר, so the כהן must prove his claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: our משנה
A non-Jew who converted to Judaism
Exempt / obligated
A case of doubt
Whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring proof

steps.whyThisMatters: It applies the general rule of הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה to מתנות כהונה, treating the כהן like any claimant.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר וְהָיְתָה לוֹ פָּרָה,
phrases.english: MISHNA: A convert who converted, and he had a cow,
if it was slaughtered before he converted, he is exempt,
after he converted, he is obligated,
if it is unclear, he is exempt,
because whoever takes from his fellow must bring the proof.
phrases.notes: Here the one trying to take is the כהן, so he needs the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר וְהָיְתָה לוֹ פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new case, after the discussion of the butcher case ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtered before conversion: exempt; after: obligated; in doubt: exempt, since the claimant must bring proof.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: when in doubt, exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that ריש לקיש noted that our משנה says 'if unsure, exempt,' which shows that a doubt is treated leniently. This sets up a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: When רב דימי came, he said: ריש לקיש raised a contradiction to רבי יוחנן. We learned in the משנה, 'if unsure, he is exempt.' This shows that a doubt is treated leniently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה's last line and pulls out a general rule: in a case of doubt, we are lenient. This is a setup line, and the next step will bring a source that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה ruled that a גר who is not sure when his cow was slaughtered does not have to give the gifts. ריש לקיש turns that ruling into a principle, ספיקא לקולא. He needs that principle in place so he can show where it clashes with another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a contradiction, meaning he pointed out two sources that seem to clash
If it is unsure, he is exempt
Evidently, this shows that
A doubt is treated leniently

phrases.english: GEMARA
When Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן –
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish raised a contradiction to Rabbi Yochanan:
We learned: "if unsure, he is exempt,"
phrases.notes: This is the last line of our משנה about the גר, from step 11.

phrases.english: evidently, a doubt is treated leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the ruling in step 11 that a doubtful case is exempt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה, a case of doubt about the gifts is treated leniently.

steps.title: Ant holes in the field: doubtful gleanings go to the poor
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about grain found in ant holes quotes רבי מאיר as saying that doubtful לקט is still לקט and belongs to the poor. That is a strict ruling about a doubt, which seems to contradict the lenient rule in step 12.
steps.simpleTranslation: But compare: grain in ant holes inside the standing crop belongs to the owner. In ant holes behind the harvesters, the upper grain goes to the poor and the lower grain belongs to the owner. רבי מאיר says: all of it goes to the poor, because doubtful לקט is considered לקט.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a source where a doubt is treated strictly: רבי מאיר gives doubtful gleanings to the poor. This seems to clash with 'if unsure, exempt.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the harvested area, the grain at the top of the hole probably fell during the harvest, so it is לקט. The grain lower down may have been gathered by the ants before the harvest, so its status is doubtful. רבי מאיר still gives it to the poor, which is strict in a case of doubt. The clash seems to assume that our unattributed משנה follows רבי מאיר, and that gifts to the poor and gifts to the כהן work the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: But contrast it with this other source
Ant holes
Standing grain that has not yet been cut
The owner of the field
Gleanings: stalks that fall during the harvest and must be left for the poor

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying that all doubts are strict everywhere. He is ruling only about gifts to the poor. The challenge works only because it compares the gifts for the poor to the gifts for the כהן.

phrases.english: But contrast it with:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת פאה (4:11).

phrases.english: Ant holes that are inside the standing grain —
these belong to the owner;
and those behind the harvesters —
the upper ones go to the poor,
and the lower ones belong to the owner.
Rabbi Meir says: all of it goes to the poor,
for doubtful gleanings are gleanings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that treats a doubt strictly, against the lenient principle drawn in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle drawn from our משנה, ספיקא לקולא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר rules that doubtful לקט goes to the poor, which is strict. If our משנה also follows רבי מאיר, he would contradict himself about gifts that must be given away when there is a doubt.

steps.title: That opinion of רבי מאיר comes from only one report
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the strict ruling is reported in רבי מאיר's name by only one חכם, רבי יהודה בן אגרא, so it is not a solid contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do not trouble me, because I learn that ruling as the view of a single person. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה בן אגרא says in the name of רבי מאיר: doubtful לקט is לקט, doubtful שכחה is שכחה, doubtful פאה is פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes away the contradiction. The strict ruling about doubtful gifts to the poor is a lone report in רבי מאיר's name, not his firmly established view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on that ruling truly being רבי מאיר's opinion. רבי יוחנן shows that it rests on one חכם's testimony alone, a ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן אגרא. Because it is a single report, it cannot override the clear ruling of our משנה that a doubt means exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not trouble or provoke me
In the name of a single person, meaning a lone opinion or report
Forgotten sheaves, which must be left for the poor
The corner of the field, which must be left for the poor

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's first answer: the strict 'doubtful לקט is לקט' is only one חכם's report of רבי מאיר. The next step shows ריש לקיש rejecting this answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do not trouble me,
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is answering ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: for I learn it as the words of a single person,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
doubtful gleanings are gleanings,
doubtful forgotten sheaves are forgotten sheaves,
doubtful corner-crop is corner-crop.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַל תַּקְנִיטֵנִי, שֶׁבִּלְשׁוֹן יָחִיד אֲנִי שׁוֹנֶה אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 13 by weakening the source of רבי מאיר's strict ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution answer: the opposing ruling is a single חכם's report, not a firmly established opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר clearly holds that doubtful gifts must be given, which would contradict our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict ruling comes only from רבי יהודה בן אגרא's report, so our משנה's rule that a doubt means exempt stands.

steps.title: ריש לקיש says the strict ruling has a real reason
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש tells רבי יוחנן that even if the strict ruling came from one obscure person, it still has a solid reason behind it, so the contradiction stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even if you teach it only in the words of בן תדל, isn't there a stated reason for it?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer from step 14. He says it does not matter who reported the strict ruling, because the ruling has a real reason, and he is about to quote it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן tried to weaken the strict ruling by saying only one חכם reported it. ריש לקיש replies that the ruling does not depend on who said it, since it is backed by a reason. So the contradiction between strict for the poor and lenient for the כהן comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: He is giving a reason. The ruling is based on logic or a source, not just on who said it.
Even if you teach it (literally: do not teach it except...).

phrases.english: He said to him: Even if you teach it
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is speaking to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: only in the language of ben Tedal,
phrases.notes: Even if you credit it to some little-known person, the question still stands.

phrases.english: isn't there a stated reason for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ אַל תִּשְׁנֶה אוֹתָהּ אֶלָּא בִּלְשׁוֹן בֶּן תַּדָּל, וְהָא טַעְמָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוחנן's answer from step 14 and restores the contradiction from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's answer that the strict ruling about doubtful לקט is weak because only one חכם reported it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling backed by a real reason cannot be brushed aside just because of who reported it.

steps.title: The verse teaches: be generous to the poor from your own
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the reason. The פסוק 'do justice to the poor' cannot mean bending court rulings, so it must mean giving the poor your own property when in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: What does the verse 'Do justice to the poor and needy' mean? What is 'do justice'? If you say it means in court cases, isn't it written 'Do not favor a poor man in his case'? Rather, it means: be righteous with what is yours and give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings the source for being strict with doubts about gifts to the poor. He reads a פסוק and shows it must mean giving the poor from your own property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הצדיקו cannot mean favoring the poor in court, because another פסוק forbids that. So it must mean that when something might belong to the poor, you should give it to them from what is yours. This gives doubtful לקט a strict rule, which makes the lenient rule for מתנות כהונה stand out even more.

keyTerms.meaning: Do justice / treat as righteous.
If you say. This introduces a possible reading that will be rejected.
Do not favor him in his court case.
Be righteous with what is yours and give it to him.

steps.whyThisMatters: This source is why doubts about gifts to the poor are treated strictly. That is exactly why the contrast with the gifts to the כהן needs an explanation.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
What is meant by what is written: 'Do justice to the poor and needy'?
phrases.notes: תהלים 82:3

phrases.english: What does 'do justice' mean?
If you say it means in court judgments,
but isn't it written: 'Do not favor a poor man in his case'?
phrases.notes: שמות 23:3

phrases.english: Rather: be righteous with what is yours and give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason that ריש לקיש mentioned in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That being strict with doubts about gifts to the poor has a real basis.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 82:3, read in light of שמות 23:3.

steps.title: The cow starts exempt and the crop starts obligated
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction. Each case follows its starting status: the convert's cow began exempt, while the standing grain began obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Here, the cow stands in a presumption of exemption, while the standing grain stands in a presumption of obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to the contradiction. He explains that each doubt follows how the item started out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the man converted, his cow was not obligated in the gifts, so when we are unsure we leave it exempt. Grain growing in the field is obligated in לקט from the start, so when we are unsure it stays obligated. The difference is not about poor people versus כהנים. It is about which חזקה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: In a presumed status of being exempt.
In a presumed status of being obligated.
Standing grain still growing in the field.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about the פסוק ריש לקיש quoted. He is explaining the different outcomes through the starting status of each item.

phrases.english: Rava said: Here,
phrases.notes: Here means the case of the convert's cow and the gifts to the כהן.

phrases.english: the cow stands in a presumption of exemption,
standing grain stands in a presumption of obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָכָא, פָּרָה בְּחֶזְקַת פְּטוּרָה קָיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new resolution after ריש לקיש rejected רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases by their starting status (חזקה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Doubts about gifts to the poor and gifts to the כהן seem to follow opposite rules for no clear reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each doubt follows its original status: the cow is presumed exempt and the crop is presumed obligated.

steps.title: אביי challenges from a convert's dough
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that a convert's dough also starts out exempt, yet when there is a doubt, the convert must separate חלה. This goes against רבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But dough made before he converted is exempt from חלה, after he converted it is obligated, and if there is a doubt it is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's answer with a case that has the same starting status but a strict outcome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough belonging to a non-Jew is exempt from חלה, so by רבא's logic a convert's dough should stay presumed exempt when there is a doubt. Yet the rule is that he is obligated. So the starting status alone does not seem to decide the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough.
The portion of dough given to a כהן.
He converted.
If there is a doubt, he is obligated.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי עִיסָּה נַעֲשֵׂית עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּיֵּיר –
phrases.english: But there is dough: if it was made before he converted,
he is exempt from חלה;
if made after he converted, he is obligated;
if there is a doubt, he is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וַהֲרֵי עִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's חזקה answer from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a convert's property, which started out exempt, stays exempt when there is a doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dough made by a non-Jew also starts out exempt, yet the doubtful case is strict, so the starting status cannot be what decides the outcome.

steps.title: Doubts about prohibitions are strict, doubts about money are lenient
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers אביי. חלה is different from the priestly gifts because a doubt about חלה involves a prohibition, and in such a doubt we are strict. A doubt about the gifts is only about money, so we are lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A doubt about a prohibition, we go strict. A doubt about money, we go lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his rule against אביי's challenge about the convert's dough. He explains that חלה is a different kind of doubt from the cow's gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating חלה is forbidden to anyone who is not a כהן, so a doubt about חלה is a doubt about a prohibition, and we must be strict even though the dough started out exempt. The cow's gifts are just money owed to a כהן, so the convert can rely on the cow's exempt starting point and keep them. The 'starting status' rule still works, but only for money cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about something forbidden: be strict.
A doubt about money: be lenient, so the person holding it keeps it.
A prohibition, something forbidden by the Torah.
Money or property matters.

steps.whatToRemember: This is a basic rule across all of ש״ס: doubts about איסור go לחומרא, and doubts about ממון go לקולא. It explains why the convert's חלה and his cow's gifts come out differently.
steps.whyThisMatters: It narrows רבא's rule from step 17. The starting status decides money cases, but a doubt about a prohibition requires strictness no matter how the item started.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבא answering אביי's question about the convert's dough.

phrases.english: A doubt about a prohibition, go strict;
a doubt about money, go lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סְפֵק אִיסּוּרָא לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 18 by sorting the cases into prohibition doubts and money doubts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the cases: a prohibition doubt versus a money doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the convert's dough should be exempt, like the cow, since both started out exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The starting-status rule applies to money doubts like the priestly gifts. חלה involves a prohibition, so we are strict even though the dough started out exempt.

steps.title: Eight doubts for a convert, and the four where he is obligated
steps.stepSummary: רבא's answer is supported by רב חסדא and a ברייתא of רבי חייא. There are eight doubtful cases for a גר: four obligate him and four exempt him. The four obligating cases are his wife's offering, חלה, a firstborn non-kosher animal, and a firstborn kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said, and so רבי חייא teaches: Eight doubts were stated about a convert, four for obligation and four for exemption. His wife's offering, חלה, the firstborn of a non-kosher animal, and the firstborn of a kosher animal: these are for obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that backs up רבא's split. It begins listing the doubts of a convert, starting with the four cases where he is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these four cases involves a prohibition, so the convert is strict and treats himself as obligated, exactly as רבא said. חלה appears on the obligated list, which directly confirms רבא's answer to אביי. The four exempt cases come next and should be the money cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight cases of doubt.
Obligated / exempt.
His wife's offering, brought after giving birth.
The firstborn of a non-kosher animal, meaning a donkey.
The firstborn of a kosher animal, which is holy.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists. Here the convert is OBLIGATED, because each case involves a prohibition. The exempt cases come later and are the money cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבא's distinction is not a new idea made up to answer אביי. An earlier teaching already sorted a convert's doubts this way.

phrases.english: As Rav Chisda said,
and so Rabbi Chiya teaches:
Eight doubts were stated about a convert,
phrases.notes: Each doubt is whether the event happened before he converted or after.

phrases.english: four for obligation and four for exemption.
His wife's offering, and חלה,
and the firstborn of a non-kosher animal,
and the firstborn of a kosher animal: these are for obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's distinction in step 19 with an earlier teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule: be strict in a doubt about a prohibition, such as חלה, and lenient in a doubt about money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב חסדא and the ברייתא of רבי חייא listing a convert's eight doubts, with חלה among the obligated cases.
